newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: The following matches are being played in the Spanish league championship this weekend: (league positions in parentheses, all kickoff times GMT)

Deportivo's week of internal upheaval has contrasted with the euphoria at first division newcomers Extremadura after the club's first away win. Potentially treacherous pitch conditions add to the likelihood of an upset.
Vicente Miera will be looking for his first away win as Espanyol manager against a Valencia side without midfielder Valery Karpin and defender Francisco Ferreira, who are both suspended.
Real will hope not to come back to earth with a bump after the spectacular derby win at Atletico, and will be without suspended striker Predrag Mijatovic, who was sent off in that game.
Hercules were knocked out of the Cup in midweek after consecutive league victories, while Athletic have lost their way in the past few games. Another game with possible pitch problems.
Brazilian playmaker Giovanni should be fit to play in a match in which Bobby Robson's Barcelona hope to bury memories of the disatrous defeat by Hercules two weeks ago.
With successive league and Cup defeats complicating the club's perennial perennial turmoil, Sevilla will again look to newly-signed Croatian playmaker Robert Prosinecki for inspiration.

Real Sociedad, the most in-form side in Spain, will replace injured Romanian striker Gheorghe Craioveanu with Mutiu Adepoju for the game at struggling Logrones, a team that has already fired two coaches this season.

Tenerife forward Meho Kodro will miss the game through injury, while Atletico's Juan Eduardo Esnaider is one of several stars who could be sidelined as Radomir Antic -- who has never lost at Tenerife -- looks to turn around his team.
Zaragoza will be without star striker Gustavo Poyet and defender Kily Gonzalez in a fixture that they have lost in the past two season.

The derby game in the northern region of Asturias has been preceded by a round of verbal clashes between representatives of the two clubs. But pride isn't the only thing at stake, as both sides badly need the points to clear the relegation zone.
Betis defensive giant Roberto Rios returns from suspension as the southerners try to restart their championship challenge against this season's surprise outfit.
